captions.cache-reconciliation: Expert entry reconciliation and separate cache gauges in storage-demand TP1 middle -02. The 11,519 uploads minus 11,455 evictions equal 64 entries, matching the last observed resident-entry gauge; the implied initial occupancy is zero, not independently measured. Subsequent observed boundaries satisfy the entry balance. The recorded cache.peak_bytes value, 209.574 MiB, is the cache charged-byte high-water (resident + pending + scratch), bounded by ExpertCacheLimits.max_bytes = 320 MiB, a cache accounting ceiling, not owner physical memory. No independently recorded owner physical peak or owner physical ceiling is available; no contradiction is implied. Invocation gauges and lifetime peaks are not accumulated across invocations or a final owner ledger.
captions.invocation-timeline: Per-invocation expert upload/eviction deltas and resident-entry observations for the 30 completed invocations in storage-demand TP1 middle -02. Serialized request/log-byte anchors assign the 3/9/9/9 invocations to requests. The x-axis is log-order invocation ordinal, not elapsed time, output-token index, or transaction-as-request ID. Entry occupancy is observed only at invocation completion, not continuously; uploads are not inferred cache misses.
captions.logical-transfer: Paired logical checkpoint-reader and facade H2D byte deltas for four serialized requests in storage-demand TP1 middle -02. GiB means 2^30 bytes; the right panel resolves the small H2D-minus-reader differences in KiB (2^10 bytes). These are application counters, not physical storage I/O or physical bus traffic; startup I/O is outside invocation accounting.
captions.timing: Launch-to-ready startup and per-request HTTP TTFT/E2E in the single successful DEBUG-instrumented storage-demand TP1 middle -02 run (n=1). TTFT is send to first nonempty SSE content; E2E is send to EOF. Startup has a different origin and is not part of the request bars. Instrumentation overhead is unmeasured; there are no statistics, confidence intervals, kernel timings, or comparative speedups.

caveats: One successful instrumented run (n=1), not independent repetitions; no statistics or confidence intervals.
ferrule_performance DEBUG overhead is unmeasured; these latencies are not a fast baseline or comparable vLLM throughput.
Read calls/bytes are logical checkpoint-reader/syscall counters; physical NAS/NFS IO and OS page-cache state are unknown.
H2D/artifact counters are facade activity, not physical bus traffic or device-kernel timing. Startup IO is not covered by invocation sums.
Expert uploads are not cache misses. Misses and IO credits are unobserved, not inferred from hits/uploads.
SSE text/usage matches are not generated-token-ID or logits evidence; frozen reference IDs are never observed generated IDs.
TTFT is send-to-first-nonempty-SSE content; E2E is send-to-EOF; TPOT is the recorded content-event/usage proxy, not exact token time.
Cache occupancy/scratch/owner-peak fields are gauges: last invocation and observed maxima, never additive deltas or a final ledger.
Memory values are independent sampled component maxima, not an additive decomposition, exact peak, hard cap, or continuous coverage.
Anonymous is resident anonymous memory, not PssAnon. PssAnon/PssFile and physical host cap are unobserved.
GPU memory is selected-device aggregate telemetry; owned-process attribution and absence of foreign interference remain unproven.
After-first-request samples include later canaries, not steady state. Shutdown resource_contract_complete is unknown despite exit/custody/idle evidence.
